def serve_file(
    *,
    doc: Document,
    use_archive: bool,
    disposition: str,
    follow_formatting: bool = False,
) -> FileResponse:
    if use_archive:
        if TYPE_CHECKING:
            assert doc.archive_filename

        file_handle = doc.archive_file
        filename = (
            doc.archive_filename
            if follow_formatting
            else doc.get_public_filename(archive=True)
        )
        mime_type = "application/pdf"
    else:
        if TYPE_CHECKING:
            assert doc.filename

        file_handle = doc.source_file
        filename = doc.filename if follow_formatting else doc.get_public_filename()
        mime_type = doc.mime_type
        # Support browser previewing csv files by using text mime type
        if mime_type in {"application/csv", "text/csv"} and disposition == "inline":
            mime_type = "text/plain"
        # Tell browsers to use UTF-8 for the text files we parse as UTF-8
        if mime_type in {"text/plain", "text/csv", "application/csv"}:
            mime_type = f"{mime_type}; charset=utf-8"

    response = FileResponse(file_handle, content_type=mime_type)
    # Firefox is not able to handle unicode characters in filename field
    # RFC 5987 addresses this issue
    # see https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5987#section-4.2
    # Chromium cannot handle commas in the filename
    filename_normalized = (
        normalize("NFKD", filename.replace(",", "_"))
        .encode(
            "ascii",
            "ignore",
        )
        .decode("ascii")
        .replace("\\", "_")
        .replace('"', "_")
    )
    filename_encoded = quote(filename)
    content_disposition = (
        f"{disposition}; "
        f'filename="{filename_normalized}"; '
        f"filename*=utf-8''{filename_encoded}"
    )
    response["Content-Disposition"] = content_disposition
    return response

def serve_file(
    *,
    doc: Document,
    use_archive: bool,
    disposition: str,
    follow_formatting: bool = False,
) -> FileResponse:
    if use_archive:
        if TYPE_CHECKING:
            assert doc.archive_filename

        file_handle = doc.archive_file
        filename = (
            doc.archive_filename
            if follow_formatting
            else doc.get_public_filename(archive=True)
        )
        mime_type = "application/pdf"
    else:
        if TYPE_CHECKING:
            assert doc.filename

        file_handle = doc.source_file
        filename = doc.filename if follow_formatting else doc.get_public_filename()
        mime_type = doc.mime_type
        # Support browser previewing csv files by using text mime type
        if mime_type in {"application/csv", "text/csv"} and disposition == "inline":
            mime_type = "text/plain"
        # Tell browsers to use UTF-8 for the text files we parse as UTF-8
        if mime_type in {"text/plain", "text/csv", "application/csv"}:
            mime_type = f"{mime_type}; charset=utf-8"

    response = FileResponse(file_handle, content_type=mime_type)
    # Firefox is not able to handle unicode characters in filename field
    # RFC 5987 addresses this issue
    # see https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5987#section-4.2
    # Chromium cannot handle commas in the filename
    filename_normalized = (
        normalize("NFKD", filename.replace(",", "_"))
        .encode(
            "ascii",
            "ignore",
        )
        .decode("ascii")
        .replace("\\", "_")
        .replace('"', "_")
    )
    filename_encoded = quote(filename)
    content_disposition = (
        f"{disposition}; "
        f'filename="{filename_normalized}"; '
        f"filename*=utf-8''{filename_encoded}"
    )
    response["Content-Disposition"] = content_disposition
    return response

file_response resolves a request/root pair, stops on a forbidden resolution, derives an effective file document, and delegates serving that document to serve_file.

The action body contains no explicit permission decision; file_response and its resolution helper contain the visible downstream control before serving.
DRF authentication and view/object permission classes configured on DocumentViewSet are upstream controls for the action.

rules.claim: The DocumentViewSet Download action is an authenticated detail action whose entry receives the path identifier pk, delegates to file_response(pk, request, "attachment"), and converts FileNotFoundError or Document.DoesNotExist into HTTP 404.

The Download action does not itself extract or validate a version parameter; it passes the path identifier and request unchanged to file_response, so version resolution is delegated to that downstream path.
file_response resolves a request/root pair, stops on a forbidden resolution, derives an effective file document, and delegates serving that document to serve_file.
The detail GET download action calls file_response with attachment disposition; missing document or file exceptions are translated to HTTP 404.

When request_doc and root_doc resolve and the explicit root permission check does not return HttpResponseForbidden, the representation path continues to _get_effective_file_doc and then serve_file; this helper does not itself choose the original versus archive representation.
When the explicit root permission check fails, _resolve_request_and_root_doc returns HttpResponseForbidden and file_response returns it before effective file-document selection or file opening.
The explicit guard evaluates has_perms_owner_aware(request.user, "view_document", root_doc). If the check succeeds, file_response proceeds to effective file-document selection and serve_file.

If request.user is non-null and has_perms_owner_aware(request.user, "view_document", root_doc) is false, _resolve_request_and_root_doc returns HttpResponseForbidden; file_response returns that response and does not open a file.
After the root-view guard succeeds, file_response passes the separately selected file_doc to serve_file; no additional file_doc permission check is visible in the shown chain.

_resolve_request_and_root_doc binds the path-selected request_doc separately from the derived root_doc; it uses the global manager when include_deleted is true and returns either a forbidden response or the pair for subsequent file selection.

The download chain supplies request.user to the explicit has_perms_owner_aware check; the viewset source also declares IsAuthenticated and PaperlessObjectPermissions, while this helper's direct check is visible in file_response's resolution path.
The explicit download-chain permission check is bound to root_doc returned by _resolve_request_and_root_doc, not directly to request_doc or to the later file_doc.

dependencies.reason: The helper determines the request document and root document and can return the forbidden short-circuit before any file is served.
The helper selects the concrete Document object whose file representation is passed to serve_file.
This helper controls whether an available archive representation is selected instead of the original representation.
serve_file opens the selected representation and determines the response metadata and filename.
The action body contains no explicit permission decision; file_response and its resolution helper contain the visible downstream control before serving.
DRF authentication and view/object permission classes configured on DocumentViewSet are upstream controls for the action.

The selected file document is determined after request/root resolution and is the resource whose representation is later served; the source body of _get_effective_file_doc is already shown and must govern this relationship.
The exact global-permission, ownership, owner-null, and object-grant branches depend on the helper implementation; the shown caller establishes only that root_doc is the checked object.

Authentication and DRF permission-class enforcement are configured on the viewset, but the supplied source window does not include the declaration or dispatch implementation needed to close that upstream control.

behavior.explanation: The path parameter identifies request_doc, but the returned object is file_doc, not necessarily request_doc. If the path identifies a version and no version parameter is supplied, file_doc is request_doc. If the path identifies a root, or any version parameter is supplied, the code resolves a file document from root_doc. Permission failure prevents file selection; missing documents or files produce HTTP 404.

observations.subject: file_response
observations.claim: The path primary key first resolves request_doc through Document.global_objects because file_response requests include_deleted=True. The code then separately resolves root_doc and separately computes file_doc; these objects are not automatically identical.

observations.subject: _get_effective_file_doc
observations.claim: If the path identifies a version document and no version parameter is supplied, request_doc itself becomes file_doc. Otherwise the effective file document is resolved relative to root_doc.

observations.subject: DocumentViewSet.file_response
observations.object: selected file document and serve_file response
observations.claim: file_response resolves request_doc/root_doc, obtains file_doc, then calls serve_file. Archive use is false when original_requested is true; otherwise it is true only when file_doc.has_archive_version is true. follow_formatting is passed directly from request.query_params.

observations.subject: serve_file
observations.claim: serve_file opens file_doc.archive_file in archive mode or file_doc.source_file in source mode. Archive mode uses application/pdf. Source mode uses file_doc.mime_type, with text/CSV adjustments. follow_formatting selects stored filename metadata; otherwise get_public_filename is used. Filename normalization affects the response header, not the opened handle.

observations.subject: DocumentViewSet and _resolve_request_and_root_doc
observations.claim: The viewset source declares IsAuthenticated and PaperlessObjectPermissions; the explicit download-chain check passes request.user to has_perms_owner_aware.

observations.subject: has_perms_owner_aware(request.user, "view_document", root_doc)
observations.claim: Before file_doc is selected or opened, the explicit check is against root_doc. Failure returns HttpResponseForbidden and file_response returns without calling serve_file.

observations.subject: authorization versus returned file
observations.claim: The source-visible authorization object can differ from the file-owning object. In the definite version-path/no-version-parameter branch, root_doc is checked while request_doc, the version document, supplies the file to serve_file.
